source_title: ‘Beyond the Gates’ Star Tamara Tunie Dedicates Her First Daytime Emmy Win to Her Mom, 92: ‘I Love You, Mommy’ - People.com
source_excerpt:
“My heart is so full right now. This is the best welcome back to daytime ever,” the actress began her acceptance speech at the 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards
Tamara Tunie won her first-ever Daytime Emmy Award for her portrayal of Anita Dupree in Beyond the Gates
Tunie took home Outstanding Lead Actress in a Daytime Drama Series at the ceremony on Friday, Oct. 30
Other nominees included Stacy Haiduk, Karla Mosley, Michelle Stafford and Heather Tom
Tamara Tunie celebrated her mother while accepting her first Emmy trophy.
The actress, 67, won Outstanding Lead Actress in a Daytime Drama Series for her portrayal of Anita Dupree in Beyond the Gates at the 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards on Friday, Oct. 30. This is her first-ever Emmy win in her decades-long career. After a standing ovation, Tunie began her speech, “My heart is so full right now.”
“This is the best welcome back to daytime ever,” Tunie continued. “There is a host of Black actresses who paved the way for me, and I feel them as I stand here tonight, beginning with the legendary Cicely Tyson, the first Black woman to appear on a daytime television show, The Guiding Light .”
“Congratulations to my sister nominees, especially my TV wild child, Danny, who is portrayed by the beaming light that is Karla Mosley ,” she said. “I am so honored to be in the company of you formidable women. Man, we had a ball the other night. There was a lot of wine and a lot of food, and we were solving all the problems of the world.”
Tunie went on to thank the Academy, her colleagues, her team and fans of soap operas and Beyond the Gates . She shared her gratitude to the “best cast and crew that bring dedication and joy to the studio every single day.”
“I get to share the camera with the legendary Mr. Clifton Davis, the best, most loving husband on daytime television,” she said of the actor, who stars as Vernon Dupree.
“Every play, every TV show, every movie, every performance has led me to this evening,” she continued, “A sincere thank you to every director, every actor, every producer and every crew member I have worked with over the years. I have carried what you taught me forward to the next project as I continue my growth as a storyteller.”
Tunie thanked her family for their “love and pride in my accomplishments,” and gave a special shout-out to her mother, Evelyn, who was in the crowd at the ceremony.
“There is one person who has been on this journey with me every single step of the way, who has traveled across states, countries and oceans to support my dream. I would not be who I am as an actor or a woman without her love, support, encouragement and mere presence,” she said. “She has been my example, my role model and my inspiration. I accept this honor on behalf of my mother ... who, at 92 years young, crossed the country yet again to see me take this goal tonight. I love you, mommy!”
In Beyond the Gates , Tunie stars as Anita, the glamorous matriarch of the Dupree dynasty. Speaking to Gold Derby about her first-ever Daytime Emmy nomination, Tunie said, “It feels wonderful.”
“It’s an incredible mixed bag. I’m so honored, first and foremost, to be acknowledged,” she continued. “I’m thrilled for my show. I’m thrilled for the 15 nominations that we received, and I’m thrilled for my other castmates. We’ve all been working so hard, and it’s great to be recognized.”
Other nominees included Stacy Haiduk for Days of Our Lives , Mosley for Beyond the Gates , Michelle Stafford for The Young and the Restless, and Heather Tom for The Bold and the Beautiful .
Haiduk, 58, stars as Kristen DiMera, the manipulative but fiercely loyal daughter of Stefano DiMera and Rachel Blake, in Days of Our Lives . The actress joined the beloved soap opera in 2018 and also portrays Susan Banks, Kristen’s eccentric lookalike.
Her nomination at this year’s ceremony marks her first lead actress nod at the Daytime Emmys and her fourth overall. Speaking to TV Insider on her career milestone, Haiduk said she’s “so grateful” for her nomination.
“Every moment I have the chance to just look up at the universe and say thank you, I take it,” she continued. “I was not expecting this year to go the way it has, so I’m pleasantly surprised at the journey that I’ve been on.”
Mosley, 45, stars as Dani Dupree, the unapologetic younger daughter of Vernon and Anita Dupree in Beyond the Gates . The show follows the lives of a wealthy Black dynasty, the Dupree family, as they navigate love, legacy and long-held secrets.
At this year’s Daytime Emmys, Beyond the Gates earned 15 total nominations, including Outstanding Daytime Drama Series. In an interview with Soap Opera Digest , Mosley admitted she has the “biggest perma-grin” on her face when she found out she’d been nominated. Her joy only grew when she learned just how many nods the show got.
“We all worked so hard, and in some ways, this was not the little engine, but that big steam train that could,” Mosley said. “Everyone puts in not just time, but care and heart. As the nominations were coming out, we were all together, screaming and hugging each other in the hair and makeup room. It was so exciting.”
In The Young and the Restless , Stafford, 61, portrays Phyllis Summers. She debuted on the soap opera in 1994 and impressed producers enough that they gave her a contract to periodically reprise her role. Over the years, Stafford has received 14 Daytime Emmy nominations and previously won in 1997, 2004 and 2024.
“They all feel different,” she told TV Insider of her nominations. “They really do because you’re at a different place in your life. In 1996 [her first nomination], that was a complete shock; I felt like I hadn’t been on the show long enough to have earned that. And every single time, I’m never expecting it, so it’s just a different kind of shock now.”
Tom, 50, portrays Katie Logan, the fierce businesswoman and head of Logan Designs, in The Bold and the Beautiful . In 2012, the six-time Emmy-winning actress set the record for the only actress in television history to win an Emmy in all three performer categories: Younger, Supporting and Lead Actress. Tom tied the record for the most Emmys won by an actress in a Daytime Drama Series with Erika Slezak ( One Life to Live ) in 2020.
